tags.chapter_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

question.text: Group-<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>13</mn></math> elements react with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in amorphous form to form oxides of type <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mo>=</mo></math> element). Which among the following is the most basic oxide?

solution.text:
The basicity of an oxide is closely related to the electropositive character of the element. The more electropositive the element, the more basic its oxide will be. This is because the oxide ion can react with a cation to form a basic oxide. As we move down Group 13, the electropositive character of the elements increases, and so does the basicity of their oxides.

B2O3<Al2O3<Ga2O3<In2O3<Tl2O3

So most basic oxide among the given options is Tl2O3.
